metodologi.title: Methodology
metodologi.lead: How we join R3P damage figures to kab/kota and village geometries — rewritten from the Aceh Tangguh inventory pipeline, not copied from other projects.

s1.title: R3P damage aggregation
s1.body: Choropleth values come from Compiled R3P: light, moderate, and heavy housing damage (RR+RS+RB) rolled up by kab/kota and by village. At kab level, village rows aggregate to all 23 Aceh kab/kota; every Drive kab matched a GADM polygon.

s2.title: Name normalization
s2.body: Before matching, desa and kecamatan names are cleaned: prefixes such as Gp, Gampong, Desa, Kel, Meunasah, Mns, and Dusun are stripped; local abbreviations (MT, GLP, KR) expanded; Acehnese spellings unified (e.g. glumpang/glmpang, lhok→lok, oe→ue, baroh→baro, kuta/kute→kota); Roman and Arabic numerals aligned; parenthetical notes dropped. When two R3P rows collide on the same key, the higher-damage row wins.

s3.title: Village geometry join
s3.body: Primary geometry comes from Indonesian village borders for Aceh, with GADM admin4 fill-ins where needed. Matching is staged: kab+kec+desa, then kab+desa, then fuzzy within kab+kec and kab (score ≥86, near-ties rejected), plus a small manual alias map. R3P village codes are not crosswalked to GADM/Kemendagri codes because kab numbering schemes differ. After tuning, about 98.5% of R3P village rows link to geometry, with 100% damage-value coverage.

s4.title: Terciles / color buckets
s4.body: Positive values are split into three buckets (low / medium / high) using tercile thresholds. For kab: roughly 1,362 and 10,795. For villages: roughly 106 and 1,184. Those buckets drive polygon fill colors on the map.

s5.title: Limits & updates
s5.body: A small set of village names remains unmatched (ambiguous names or no reliable geometry). The Drive inventory is rebuilt via local scripts; map layers ship as GeoJSON APIs, with optional PMTiles vector tiles for performance. Homepage and map figures follow the deployed fixture snapshot.

s6.title: Aceh DIBI dashboard
s6.body: The homepage “Aceh disaster dashboard” aggregates figures from BNPB’s public DIBI dashboard (https://dibi.bnpb.go.id/superset/dashboard/2/), dataset Dampak kejadian bencana. Every query filters provinsi=Aceh and is_bencana=true, plus DIBI’s default hazard categories. This uses Apache Superset’s internal API (not the official Satu Data Bencana CKAN channel); if DIBI is unavailable the app falls back to a snapshot fixture. Housing-loss estimates follow DIBI’s million-rupiah unit.

s7.title: Basemap, performance, and Sentinel
s7.body: The map runs on MapLibre (GPU). The default operational basemap is Carto Positron raster (OSM). OpenFreeMap vector is optional (`?vector=1`) and falls back to Carto if the CDN fails — that already happened in our sandbox. HD satellite uses Esri World Imagery. The Sentinel-2 option is EOX’s annual Cloudless mosaic (Copernicus, 10 m) — a background, not “today’s” image, because Aceh is usually cloudy. Latest Sentinel-2 L2A scenes are queried via STAC (Element84) as an archive heartbeat, not as the basemap. Location points render as GPU-clustered GeoJSON, not HTML markers, so thousands of facilities stay light. Area overlays remain PMTiles. Architecture notes: docs/basemap.md.

s8.title: Homepage early warnings
s8.body: The homepage Hazard strip is replaced by Peringatan Dini: three cards (weather, MAGMA, Sipongi) that fail independently. Weather summarises the existing /api/weather stack (BMKG / Open-Meteo + snapshot) and only surfaces conditions that need attention (heavy/extreme rain, strong wind, thunderstorms); IRBI extreme-weather class is not treated as a live alert. MAGMA parses the public magma.esdm.go.id homepage feed (markersGempa), then magma.vsi.esdm.go.id if needed, and keeps Aceh events (bbox ~95–98.3E / 2–6.15N or wilayah text). If live MAGMA fails (HTTP error, WAF, timeout, or unreadable HTML), the gempa card is empty and marked delayed — the last fixture snapshot is not shown as a current event. Sipongi uses the map’s public opsroom GeoJSON (indoHotspot), Aceh only, medium/high confidence; a Sipongi live-fetch failure still shows the last fixture snapshot plus a delayed-data label. Earthquake and hotspot numbers are never invented. GET /api/hazards and map ?hazard= aliases remain.
